buttonLabel: "Adventures through Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru"
lead: >-
  This selection brings together Iguazu, the Atacama, the road to Cusco, Machu Picchu and the mountains around Medellín. The full 32-day itinerary also includes the most demanding high-altitude stage: a 4×4 journey past Bolivian lagoons towards Uyuni. Machu Picchu, however, is visited by train rather than via the Inca Trail. We explain the real physical demands and travel sequence to distinguish genuine adventures from scenic but more relaxed sightseeing days.
---

## What the Adventure filter means for these four countries

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru among the main countries and adventure as a significant theme. The [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Ecuador. **The selected countries form part of the complete itinerary, not a separate shortened four-country programme.**

The most travel-intensive days lie across national borders: after Chile's Atacama, travellers cross Bolivia's highlands before continuing past Titicaca into Peru. Within the four selected countries, the tour offers waterfall walks, sightseeing routes through Andean cities and excursions to archaeological sites. The [four-country geographical catalogue](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_peru/) and [general multi-country adventure selection](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) can help you compare other programmes.

## Brazil: walks at Iguazu and an optional paid activity on the water

After [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itinerary continues to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). A group excursion explores the Brazilian side of the falls, following the cascades and viewpoints. This is a nature sightseeing day on walking paths; a long sporting trek through the jungle is not listed as the main service.

**Macuco Safari**, including its water-based section, can be added at extra cost. It does not replace the standard excursion and is not automatically included. The following day, the itinerary visits the Argentine side of Iguazu before continuing towards Buenos Aires. Arranging an optional visit therefore depends on the confirmed schedule and programme conditions.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama before the two-day expedition

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), travellers take a city tour before flying to Calama and transferring to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The Chilean stop is used partly for acclimatisation. The programme does not include an independent multi-day desert trek.

**The two-day off-road route begins in Bolivia**, not Chile. The 4×4 vehicles cross a plateau above 4,000 metres, passing Laguna Verde, hot springs, geysers and lagoons towards [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Plan for long drives, temperature swings, basic overnight accommodation and possible altitude sickness. Being comfortable with ordinary walks does not necessarily mean coping well at high elevations.

An optional astronomy excursion in the Atacama runs separately, depends on the lunar cycle and is not part of the off-road expedition.

## Peru: through Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu

After Bolivia, the itinerary crosses the border near Desaguadero and arrives in the [Puno and Lake Titicaca region](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Travellers visit the Uros Islands, learn about life on the lake and spend the night in Puno. A tourist bus then travels to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) with stops along the Andean road, including La Raya Pass.

Peru's major excursion is [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The programme provides **a full-day tour with an English-speaking guide and a train journey back to Cusco**. It offers an introduction to a mountain archaeological complex, but **does not specify trekking along the Inca Trail, a multi-day hike or a separate climbing product**.

Cusco sightseeing also includes Coricancha, Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuamán. A flight then takes the group to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) for an excursion around Miraflores and the historic centre. If ancient cities and architecture are your primary interest, see the [culture-focused selection for these four countries](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_peru/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Colombia: mountain views and a trip to Guatapé

The Colombian section begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). From here, a day excursion visits the [replica of old El Peñol](/colombia/place/el-penol/), [El Peñón de Guatapé rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), with its reservoir and green slopes.

Visiting the area is included, but a separate climb up El Peñón's steps is not confirmed as a mandatory paid service. Later stops at Comuna 13, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) primarily concern urban history, museums and transfers.

## Preparing for the Andean section

The most important consideration is the **sequence of altitudes**: San Pedro de Atacama, the Bolivian plateaus, La Paz, the Titicaca region and Cusco. The programme includes an acclimatisation stop, but this cannot eliminate medical risks for every traveller. Accelerating the ascent just to save a day is unwise.

For the Andes, pack layers, sun protection and prepare for long drives; understand any relevant medical restrictions. It is also worth clarifying the physical demands of particular excursions, any steps involved and the distance from transport to each site. Ada Tours can help match the genuinely included services to an interest in adventure without misrepresenting a sightseeing excursion as an imaginary trek.

Entry and transit conditions for all eight countries must also be checked, including land-border crossings, along with access permits for archaeological sites. Flights and high-altitude transfers connect the stages of the journey; changing one day without reviewing the others can be risky.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru

### Is the Inca Trail hike to Machu Picchu included?

No. This programme specifies a one-day guided visit with a train journey back to Cusco. A multi-day Inca Trail hike is not listed as a service.

### Why does an article about four countries mention Bolivia?

Because the [existing 32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers eight nations. The main high-altitude off-road stage takes place in Bolivia, after Chile and before Peru.

### Is climbing El Peñón in Colombia included?

The programme includes visiting El Peñón and Guatapé. A separate ascent is not listed as an included service.

### Is the journey suitable without athletic training?

There are many sightseeing walks, but also long transfers and elevations exceeding 4,000 metres. Discuss physical demands and individual limitations before booking.

lead: >-
  The main historical highlight of combining Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru is the heritage of the Incas: Cusco, the Coricancha temple, Sacsayhuamán and Machu Picchu. Rio and Santiago introduce the development of major capitals, while Cartagena and Bogotá explore the colonial period and pre-Columbian art. All these experiences form part of an extensive eight-country South American itinerary. Discover the included excursions, transfers and monuments that make the journey worthwhile.
---

## Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru: cultural highlights of a long journey

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the four selected main countries and the “Culture and History” theme. The [32-day South America programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Ecuador. The filter does not indicate a separate tour limited to four nations: **the historical sites form part of the complete eight-country itinerary**.

An important advantage of this journey is the opportunity to compare Inca culture with the history of colonial cities and life in modern capitals. Peru has several days dedicated to archaeology; in Chile and Brazil, excursions are shorter and focus on urban monuments. Colombia concludes with Cartagena's walls, Bogotá's museums and Zipaquirá. The [geographical catalogue for this combination](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_peru/) removes the theme filter, while the [general multi-country culture selection](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) offers other destinations.

## Brazil: discovering history through Rio de Janeiro

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), excursions with a Russian-speaking guide visit Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, as well as Sugarloaf Mountain and the city's sights. The itinerary names the São Sebastião Cathedral. This stage introduces Rio's recognisable architecture and urban history, with views across the bay and neighbourhoods by the ocean.

After Rio, the group flies to [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The waterfalls belong to the nature section, so describing the visit as an archaeological or historical excursion would be inaccurate. The Argentine side of the falls, Buenos Aires and a trip to Montevideo follow; these countries form part of the complete route even though they are absent from this selection's title.

## Chile: Santiago from La Moneda to its modern neighbourhoods

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the sightseeing tour begins in central districts, including La Moneda Palace, Plaza de Armas and surrounding historic buildings such as the cathedral. The programme then visits Santa Lucía Hill and the neighbourhoods of Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia.

In one day, travellers gain an impression of both old and modern Santiago. An optional winery excursion to the Maipo Valley with a tasting can be discussed separately, but **it is not part of the mandatory historical programme**.

After Chile, the route crosses high-altitude Bolivia. One of the important cultural stops outside the four-country filter is Tiwanaku, where the programme visits archaeological structures before continuing towards Lake Titicaca and Peru.

## Peru: the Uros Islands, Cusco and Inca architecture

The Peruvian section begins with [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). After the border crossing, travellers visit the Uros reed islands to learn about local ways of life, traditions and settlements on the lake. The next day, a tourist bus crosses the Andes towards [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), stopping along the way.

Cusco is one of the journey's principal historical centres. UNESCO recognises how the city's layout combines Inca heritage with buildings from the colonial period. The programme includes **Coricancha, Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuamán**. These are distinct sites linked to religious, engineering and public life in Andean civilisations. They are not all housed in a single museum, so the sightseeing day involves transfers and time to explore.

A separate day is devoted to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the Inca archaeological complex in the mountains. The current programme specifies an excursion with an English-speaking guide, lunch and a train journey back to Cusco. **A multi-day Inca Trail hike is not included**. Travellers enjoy a guided visit to the celebrated archaeological site without undertaking a separate sporting trek.

## Lima: colonial squares and an urban museum

After Cusco comes a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). A city tour with a Russian-speaking guide includes the Miraflores district, the Park of Love, an exterior view of Huaca Huallamarca and landmarks of the historic centre. The programme includes Plaza Mayor, Santo Domingo Monastery and a visit to the cathedral. If the cathedral is closed, the MALI Museum is an alternative.

Peru therefore reveals several eras: the living traditions of Lake Titicaca, the monumental Inca heritage of Cusco and Machu Picchu, and Lima's colonial architecture. Replacing these days with a vague promise to “discover Peruvian culture” would lose some of the route's most valuable detail.

## Colombia: Cartagena, Bogotá's museums and Zipaquirá

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the itinerary includes a tour of Comuna 13 and a visit to the Guatapé area. The journey then heads to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). During city sightseeing, travellers discover the fortifications and colonial architecture, including San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, historic streets and squares. Cartagena's fortified complex is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The final Colombian section includes [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), with La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero Collection, historic squares and views from Monserrate. A separate excursion visits [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral.

The programme identifies specific museum closures in Bogotá: the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while the Mint Museum and Botero Collection close on Tuesdays. Visit schedules must therefore be coordinated with flight dates rather than assuming every museum is available every day.

## How the historical days are distributed and what to clarify

This is an intensive itinerary, with city walks alternating with high-altitude journeys and domestic flights. The key historical priorities are **having enough time for Cusco, Machu Picchu and Colombia's museums**, without sacrificing the scheduled connections between regions.

Ada Tours can discuss sightseeing priorities, guides and additional visits based on the confirmed programme. Machu Picchu and other heritage sites have specific entry requirements and tickets for selected dates. International flights, border crossings and entry rules must be considered for all eight countries, not merely the four shown by the filter.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural journeys through Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru

### How many countries does the tour actually visit?

The [current itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers eight countries. Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru are the four countries highlighted by this thematic selection.

### Is Machu Picchu included?

Yes. A one-day excursion from Cusco with an English-speaking guide and a train journey back is scheduled. The Inca Trail trek is not included separately.

### Which archaeological sites are visited in Cusco?

The excursion includes Coricancha, Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuamán as part of a broader sightseeing day in and around the city.

### Which is better for museums: Peru or Colombia?

Peru stands out for its Inca monuments and Lima's historic centre. Colombia offers Bogotá's museums and Cartagena's colonial architecture. The choice depends on which periods of history interest you most.

buttonLabel: "Nature in Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru"
lead: >-
  Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru bring together Iguazu Falls, the dry landscapes of the Atacama, Lake Titicaca, Machu Picchu's mountain slopes and the green surroundings of Guatapé. Ada Tours offers this combination as part of an extensive 32-day journey through eight South American countries. Nature stops are interspersed with city sightseeing and flights, while the most demanding high-altitude sections also pass through Bolivia.
---

## Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru: four kinds of nature experiences

In [Brazil](/brazil/), travellers see Iguazu, where a wide river plunges into a forested gorge. [Chile](/chile/) introduces arid Andean scenery around San Pedro de Atacama. [Peru](/peru/) offers high-altitude Lake Titicaca and the sanctuary of Machu Picchu among steep slopes. [Colombia](/colombia/) adds the green hills of Antioquia, the Guatapé reservoir and panoramas of the Andes around Bogotá.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits all four, but also passes through Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Ecuador. This matters: the filter title does not mean that the ready-made journey is limited to Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru. The full geographical selection without the Nature theme is on the [four-country combination page](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_peru/).

## Brazil: a big city, mountains and waterfalls

After arriving in São Paulo, the journey begins with [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The programme includes Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the city's historic districts. Rio is fascinating for the way the ocean, mountains and neighbourhoods meet. A separate hike through Tijuca National Park is not scheduled on these days, however: nature is experienced mainly from viewpoints.

The next flight takes travellers to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where they explore the Brazilian side of the waterfalls. The walking paths offer views of the cascades and humid forest. The itinerary also visits the Argentine side of Iguazu the following day, but that belongs to a separate country within the complete eight-country journey.

Water-based activities need to be checked against the included services. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are offered at extra cost. The standard waterfall excursion does not mean a traveller automatically takes a boat ride into the spray of the falls. The national park itself is worth experiencing without those options.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama as a gateway to the Altiplano

The Chilean section starts with sightseeing in Santiago, followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The settlement lies amid one of the driest regions of the continent. The desert climate combines strong daytime sunshine with noticeable temperature swings.

On this tour, the overnight stop in San Pedro helps travellers prepare for a high-altitude vehicle journey. An optional astronomy excursion is available at an additional charge, subject to the lunar calendar. Staying close to Los Flamencos National Reserve does not mean that excursions to all its lagoons are included; listing unmentioned Chilean sites as visits would be a mistake.

After San Pedro, the route continues through Bolivia in 4×4 jeeps, visiting Laguna Verde, Laguna Colorada, geothermal areas and Uyuni. **Bolivia does not appear in this selection's title, but it is a major part of the actual sequence of nature-focused days.** It cannot be ignored when preparing for altitude or assessing the trip's duration.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu's mountain setting

From Bolivia, the route passes Tiwanaku and crosses the border towards [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) combines the lake's high-altitude natural environment with local traditions. The lake is at considerable elevation; weather, wind and temperatures on the water can differ significantly from conditions in town.

Travellers then take a tourist bus to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), with stops and lunch along the way. The next full sightseeing day focuses on [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). This is both a cultural and a natural site: the ancient city lies among steep Andean slopes in a transitional zone between the highlands and humid forests. UNESCO recognises both the historic Inca heritage and the natural value of its surrounding mountain landscape.

On the existing tour, Machu Picchu is visited as an organised excursion from Cusco with a train journey back. A multi-day Inca Trail hike, an ascent of Huayna Picchu and other mountain routes are not automatically included in the price. Access to the monument, permitted visitor circuits and tickets depends on conditions for the selected dates.

After Cusco come Lima and a flight to Ecuador. Its Galápagos nature stage is part of the complete 32-day itinerary, even though Ecuador is not included in the title of the four-country filter.

## Colombia: Guatapé reservoir and Andean terrain

The principal dedicated nature outing in Colombia runs from Medellín to [El Peñón de Guatapé rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and the [Guatapé reservoirs](/colombia/place/guatape/). A large rocky monolith rises above the water, with bays and small islands between the green shores. The excursion lasts about eight hours and includes historical and urban stops, not just time viewing the landscape.

Most of the remaining Colombian itinerary is cultural: Medellín, Comuna 13, Cartagena, Bogotá, Monserrate and Zipaquirá's Salt Cathedral. Mountains form part of the panoramas, but the tour does not include a journey into the Amazon rainforest or a multi-day visit to a national park. This distinction matters if you are choosing by the Nature theme: the label applies to the journey as a whole, not to every day.

## Altitude and physical preparation

Even if this combination attracts you for Iguazu, Titicaca, Machu Picchu and Guatapé, remember that the itinerary includes Bolivia's highlands between Chile and Peru. That section passes above 4,000 metres. Time at such elevations may cause altitude sickness regardless of ordinary athletic fitness.

Before booking, consider the full sequence: arrival in San Pedro, the journey to Laguna Verde, an overnight stay in the highlands, then Uyuni, La Paz, Puno and Cusco. Discuss health and tolerance of altitude with a doctor, and transport and route conditions with the tour organiser. Machu Picchu lies lower than certain points on this route, but that does not remove the need for acclimatisation.

## Weather and clothing for different natural regions

Tropical Iguazu, the desert Atacama, Bolivia's cold windy highlands, Lake Titicaca and Colombia's green landscapes call for different clothing. Bring a rain jacket, comfortable closed footwear, sun protection, several warm layers, lightweight clothes for hot weather and a waterproof bag for documents.

The season of particularly high water flow at the falls may not coincide with the most convenient conditions on salt flats and mountain roads. Do not expect perfect weather throughout the four highlighted countries and the other sections of the full programme. Identify your main nature priority first, then choose a practical season for the whole itinerary.

## Duration, expenses and flights

The actual tour lasts 32 days. It includes 4-star hotels, domestic flights, transfers and excursions specified in the day-by-day programme. International air tickets and optional excursions are excluded. The tour starts at $15,500 per person sharing a ½ DBL room, but that price applies to the full eight-country programme and its specified services. The same amount cannot automatically be quoted for a four-country version.

Check visa and border requirements for every country on the complete itinerary, connecting airports, passport validity and entry rules based on nationality. Hand-luggage and baggage allowances matter because the trip involves several flights within South America. A bank card that works in one city may not be accepted in every country or remote area.

If the goal is to reduce the number of countries, flights and the sequence of overnight stays must be agreed again. That is a separate travel configuration, not simply removing half the days from an already priced package.

## When to choose this combination

Brazil attracts travellers who dream of powerful waterfalls; Peru appeals to those interested in the Andes' natural scenery alongside Inca heritage; Chile suits lovers of dry mountain landscapes; Colombia offers green hills and reservoirs. One long tour combines these experiences with a cultural programme and travel between eight countries.

For comparison, see [all multi-country tours](/multi-country/) and [nature journeys](/interests/nature/). Before choosing, read the programme for each day, particularly the Bolivian highland stages and the Machu Picchu visit.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru

### Can I visit Iguazu and Machu Picchu on one trip?

Yes. Both stops are included in the [32-day programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Between them, travellers visit other countries and cross Bolivia's highlands.

### Is there a separate Inca Trail trek?

On our tour, Machu Picchu is visited on a one-day excursion from Cusco with travel by train. A multi-day Inca Trail trek is not separately specified.

### Can Bolivia's highlands be avoided?

On the existing itinerary, Chile is connected to Peru via Bolivia's 4×4 route. Removing that section would require different transport and a revised programme, so an answer is possible only after individual planning.

### Is there an Amazon excursion in Colombia?

No. The route includes Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. A separate Amazon visit is not listed.

### Is this suitable for a first trip to South America?

It offers a chance to see many countries at once, but lasts 32 days and involves flights, high altitude and frequent hotel changes. Readiness for the pace and acclimatisation matters more than previous experience of travelling in the region.

lead: >-
  On this extensive South American itinerary, Brazil offers tropical forest scenery and the option of adding the Bird Park at Iguazu; Chile brings a change of climate near the Atacama, Peru offers the high-altitude landscapes of the Andes, and Colombia connects Andean cities with the Caribbean coast. The main wildlife-watching activities on the full tour take place in Ecuador's Galápagos and at Bolivia's lagoons. We distinguish these from the scenic stops in the four selected countries.
---

## Where to watch wildlife on a journey through four countries

Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru vary considerably in climate and scenery. Yet their inclusion in the Wildlife and Safaris theme does not mean that dedicated wildlife watching is scheduled in each country.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Ecuador. It is **one eight-country programme**; the four selected countries form its thematic subset. Importantly, the Galápagos Islands, one of the principal nature sections on this long tour, are in **Ecuador**, outside the title of this page.

## Brazil: Tijuca Forest, waterfalls and the Bird Park

At the start of the programme, travellers arrive in São Paulo and then fly to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The Corcovado excursion crosses the green slopes of [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/). Here you can see how Atlantic rainforest exists beside a major city, but the excursion is primarily about Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer. A separate wildlife-watching route through Tijuca is not listed for that day.

The journey then continues to [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian-side excursion includes panoramic views of the cascades. A visit to the [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is offered **as an optional extra at $50 per person**. Travellers choosing it can encounter the region's birds in a specialist park. Visiting a bird park and observing birds in the wild are different activities and should not be confused in the tour description.

After the Brazilian-side excursion comes a visit to the waterfalls from Argentina. The chance to explore the Iguazu ecosystem thus continues in another country included on the full tour.

## Chile: Santiago and the gateway to the Atacama Desert

The Chilean section begins in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) with a city sightseeing tour, followed by a flight via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The principal natural contrast is the transition from the capital and central Chile to a dry high-altitude region.

San Pedro is the starting point for the subsequent route through high-altitude lagoons and desert landscapes in **Bolivia**. The jeep section visiting Laguna Verde, Sol de Mañana and other sites belongs to the Bolivian stage. Those lagoons should not be attributed to Chile simply because the transfer begins in San Pedro.

In Chile, the confirmed experience is discovering the Atacama as a natural region and adjusting to another climate and elevation. This programme does not specify a dedicated search for flamingos or other wild animals in Chile.

## Peru: highland nature on the way to Inca monuments

After Bolivia, the journey reaches [Puno and the Lake Titicaca region](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The itinerary visits the floating Uros Islands, then crosses high-altitude areas by tourist bus towards [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). The lake, mountain passes and changes in natural conditions are striking, but these excursions focus substantially on local people's lives and cultural heritage.

The next main stop is [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The ancient city lies among mountains and combines nature with archaeology. A standard visit to Machu Picchu, however, is not the equivalent of a multi-day trekking route, a rare-animal observation excursion or a research expedition. The programme includes a one-day trip from Cusco.

The Peruvian stage ends in Lima, followed by a flight to Ecuador. Peru's primary nature contribution here is therefore the variety of mountain landscapes between cultural sites.

## Colombia: Guatapé and the Caribbean coast

The Colombian days start after the flight from Guayaquil to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A trip to El Peñón rock and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) is scheduled, followed by an introduction to the city, Comuna 13 and a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Later stops include [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), Monserrate and Zipaquirá.

The transition between mountain scenery, urban neighbourhoods and the Caribbean coast is beautiful. But the confirmed Colombian excursions concentrate on views, history and cities. They do not include a national park visit to track wildlife, an ornithological tour or a dedicated safari. A trip specifically seeking Colombian wildlife would require a different set of destinations and days.

## Where the full tour's wildlife watching is concentrated

The eight-country journey includes a separate nature chapter on the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). In Ecuador, the itinerary visits Santa Cruz Island and follows one of two alternative sea excursions: North Seymour with Bachas Beach, or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. The specific option is selected under the programme's conditions; it would be misleading to promise all these places together.

Another stage of the full itinerary where flamingos may be seen is [Laguna Colorada in Bolivia](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Bolivia, like Ecuador, is outside the four-country selection in this page's title.

Combining Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru gives a wide range of natural environments **alongside** cultural sightseeing. A paid visit to Brazil's Bird Park can be added; Ecuador provides a distinct wildlife stage, whereas not every urban or mountain day does.

## Time, physical demands and choosing the format

The published programme lasts 32 days and involves frequent flights, sightseeing days, lengthy road sections and high-altitude transfers. When comparing tours, distinguish three things: visiting a natural site, taking part in organised wildlife watching and having time for independent hikes. These experiences are not evenly distributed on this particular itinerary.

## Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Uruguay: what connects this itinerary

This combination brings together four very different parts of South America. [Brazil](/brazil/) introduces [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). [Uruguay](/uruguay/) adds [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) across the Río de la Plata. [Chile](/chile/) features [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), while [Colombia](/colombia/) concludes the extensive journey with Andean cities and the Caribbean coast.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with all four as principal destinations. Bear in mind that **the selection means the four countries are included, not that the journey visits only those countries**. The suitable current [32-day eight-country programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. Removing any of these stages would require a separate recalculation of flights, transfers and the programme.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## How the stops are spread across the four countries

The sequence matters in practical terms. The itinerary begins in Brazil, visits Uruguay while staying in Argentina, then continues to Chile and the Andes, with Colombia forming the final stage.

| Country | Main stops |
|---|---|
| Brazil | São Paulo, Rio, Iguazu |
| Uruguay | Day trip to Montevideo |
| Chile | Santiago, Atacama |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá |

The Brazilian section begins with an arrival in São Paulo and a flight to Rio. City tours, Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and a flight to Iguazu follow. After the waterfalls, the programme moves into Argentina, where it includes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and a trip to Montevideo. Travellers fly from Buenos Aires to Santiago.

From Chile, the journey continues through Bolivia's mountain regions, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), then via the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Only after these stages do the Colombian days begin. This is fundamentally different from assuming you can simply fly from Santiago to Medellín next and complete a four-country tour.

## Brazil and Uruguay: a major city, waterfalls and the Río de la Plata

Rio and Montevideo are experienced in different ways. In Rio, the programme allocates separate days to [Christ the Redeemer](/brazil/place/corcovado-christ-the-redeemer/) and Sugarloaf Mountain. Travelling within the metropolis and queues at the main viewpoints take time, so the experiences are spread over several days. Then comes Iguazu, where both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the waterfalls are visited.

Montevideo is different. On the confirmed itinerary, it is **a one-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires**, with sightseeing and a return to Argentina in the evening. This gives travellers a chance to discover Uruguay's capital, but does not justify promising an overnight stay on its coast, Punta del Este or a comprehensive tour of the country. Anyone wanting a slower-paced exploration of Uruguay should treat that as a programme change, not an included extension.

The ferry day is particularly sensitive to timing: the morning transfer to the port, passport control, boarding, time in Montevideo and the return sailing are linked. There is a national border between Buenos Aires and Uruguay, despite the short distance on a map. We coordinate this as one complete day; it is useful to know how much free time remains after sightseeing.

## Chile: a flight to Santiago and the transition to the highlands

In Chile, the itinerary begins with a city excursion around [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is where both the scenery and travel conditions change: after humid Rio and the Río de la Plata coast, travellers arrive in a very dry climate with a wide difference between daytime and night-time temperatures.

In the Atacama, prepare for sun and wind, warm clothes for early departures and sufficient water. The next section crosses Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons by jeep. **The altitude-related demands are part of the actual eight-country tour, even though Bolivia is absent from this selection's title.** CDC medical guidance highlights the rate of ascent and adaptation to sleeping at altitude; good physical fitness alone does not rule out altitude sickness. Those with heart or lung conditions, or a history of poor tolerance of altitude, should discuss the plan with a doctor before travelling.

Entering Chile involves SAG agricultural and sanitary controls. Passengers complete a declaration concerning products of animal and plant origin and present it for inspection. This applies not only to obvious souvenirs but also to food in their luggage. The subsequent Chile–Bolivia land-border crossing likewise requires appropriate documents, ground travel arrangements and consideration of local weather restrictions.

## Colombia: three different urban experiences at the end of the journey

After Ecuador, the journey continues to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The programme includes a trip to El Peñón rock and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), a visit to Comuna 13 and a flight to the Caribbean coast. Next comes [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), where colonial buildings and the maritime climate create a very different atmosphere after the Andes.

The Colombian section finishes in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), with views from Monserrate and a separate excursion to the [Salt Cathedral in Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). The programme distinguishes sightseeing days from days with flights: travelling from Medellín to Cartagena or Cartagena to Bogotá should not automatically be regarded as a full free day. Compare not only destinations but also the number of nights in each city.

Colombia is particularly appealing to travellers who appreciate the contrasts of modern cities, mountain landscapes and the Caribbean Sea. Yet these are the closing days of a busy journey, so consider how comfortable the pace will feel after visiting the other countries and experiencing several changes of climate.

## Entry requirements, flights, cash and luggage

Because the actual itinerary covers eight countries, documents must be checked **for the whole route**, not just Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Uruguay. Requirements depend on nationality, passport type, dates and type of transit. For Russian citizens, official Russian Foreign Ministry guidance describes short visa-free visits to Colombia and Uruguay. That does not remove the need to check the other countries, flight connections and passport validity separately.

The four named countries use the Brazilian real (BRL), Chilean peso (CLP), Colombian peso (COP) and Uruguayan peso (UYU). The 32-day programme also involves the currencies of Argentina, Bolivia and Peru, while Ecuador uses the US dollar. Cash dollars are not a universal way to pay for coffee, a taxi or a small purchase. We help distinguish prepaid services from personal expenses and plan where local cash and a backup payment method may be required.

Pack lightweight clothes for tropical cities and warm layers for the Atacama and Bolivian plateau. It is practical to plan two sets of luggage: a small daypack for excursions and your main bag, observing domestic airline baggage rules. The full itinerary includes the Galápagos, so their separate biosecurity requirements must also be checked.
